issues.failure_explanation: The remark's argument (exact integration of $\tau$ because $c=A\mathbbm{1}$, and the displayed formula for $g^{(\ell;k)}$ on zero-$\tau$ arguments) covers only the nonlinear $\mathcal{G}$-terms. But eq:LTE_coeffs:y also contains $(b^T\otimes Z)(I-A\otimes Z)^{-1}(\widehat{\gamma}_i\otimes y^{(i)}(t_0))$ and $\widehat{\gamma}_i y^{(i)}(t_0)$, where $y^{(i)}=[\tilde y^{(i)};0]$ and $\tilde y^{(i)}$ contains derivatives of $r$ (e.g. $\tilde y''=\tilde J\tilde y'+\tilde g'(\tilde y)\tilde y'+r'$). Concrete counterexample: Eq:PR_Model with $\tilde J=0$, $\tilde g\equiv0$ (so $\tilde y'=r(t)$): then $\Delta g^{\{0\}}=0$ exactly and the LTE coefficients are $\widehat{\gamma}_i[r^{(i-1)}(t_0);0]$, which visibly contain $r$'s derivatives. Hence 'completely canceled' is false, and the $r$-independent (for eq:SLPR, $\lambda$-independent) error constants that this cancellation would deliver are not established: applied to the autonomized system, thm:LTE/thm:convergence have constants depending on the Lipschitz constant of the augmented $g$, which is proportional to $\|r'\|$ (for eq:SLPR, of size $|\lambda|$). Only the order of the LTE, not the stiffness-independent constants, follows from direct application.

failure_location.quote: Thus, $r$ and its derivatives are completely canceled from \cref{eq:LTE_coeffs}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the remark: state that $r$'s derivatives are canceled only from the $\mathcal{G}$-terms while remaining inside the $y^{(i)}$ inputs (bounded via Assumption 1 with $r$-dependent constants), so semilinear order still yields high order on Eq:PR_Model with constants depending on $r$'s derivatives but not on the stiffness $\tilde J$; for the specific semilinear PR test, recover stiffness-independent constants via the additional observations that the exact solution $u$ is $\lambda$-free and $\tau$ is integrated exactly.
issues.overall_effect: The stated mechanism justifying that the semilinear Prothero--Robinson test problem is 'covered by the theory' is unreliable; the promised complete cancellation of $r$ (which would give stiffness-independent error constants for PR-type problems) is false in general. The order conclusions survive only with constants depending on derivatives of $r$.

issues.failure_explanation: $R(0)=1$ for any consistent method, so $I-R(Z)$ is singular whenever $Z=hJ$ has a zero eigenvalue — e.g. $J=0$ or any singular $J$ with $\mu(J)\le0$, all allowed by the hypotheses. For such $Z$, the definitions $\xi_{n-1}=(I-R(Z))^{-1}\sum\zeta(\tau)\psi(\tau)h^{\psl+1}$ and $F(\tau;Z,t):=(I-R(Z))^{-1}\psi(\tau)[Z][t]$ are invalid, and the decomposition $y(t_n)-\widetilde y_n=(I-R(Z))\xi_{n-1}+\eta_{n-1}$ on which the telescoping/superconvergence argument rests is never established. The proof shows only that the scalar function of $z$ has a removable pole at $z=0$; it does not define $\xi_{n-1}$, nor verify the identity $(I-R(Z))F(\tau;Z,t)=\psi(\tau)[Z][t]$, for matrices $Z$ with zero eigenvalues.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $\xi_{n-1}:=\sum_{\tau\in T_{\psl+1}}\zeta(\tau)F(\tau;Z,t_{n-1})h^{\psl+1}$ where $F(\tau;z,t)$ is the rational function with the removable singularity at $z=0$ removed, and verify the rational identity $(1-R(z))F(\tau;z,t)=\psi(\tau)[z][t]$ (hence $(I-R(Z))\xi_{n-1}$ equals the leading LTE term for all admissible $Z$); the bounds eq:leading_error_function1/2 already apply to this $F$.
issues.overall_effect: The superconvergence case ($q=\psl+1$) of the main convergence theorem is unproven as written for the broad class of admissible problems with singular $J$ (including $J=0$ and the autonomized PR-type systems). issues.why_classification: The gap is confined to the definition of one auxiliary quantity in the proof; the repair uses the removable-singularity structure the proof itself establishes and changes no statement, rate, or scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The top row displays reference methods that satisfy the classical order conditions up to the respective orders ($p = 4$ for left and middle, and $p = 5$ on the right), but not any of the (other) semilinear order conditions.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims the observed slope-2 envelope of the reference methods 'match[es] the B-convergence order indicated by the theory, i.e., the error estimate thm:convergence'. The reference methods have semilinear order $\psl=1$ and classical order $p=4$ or $5$ (the same paragraph states they satisfy no semilinear order conditions beyond the trivial ones), so thm:convergence gives $q=\psl=1$ for them; the superconvergence clause $q=\psl+1$ requires $p=\psl+1=2$. The theory therefore indicates a slope-1 bound, not slope 2: the observed slope-2 envelope (a classical Prothero--Robinson result for stiffly accurate methods) exceeds, rather than matches, the paper's theorem.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose a Runge--Kutta method is A-, AS-, and ASI-stable, has classical order $p$, and semilinear order $\psl \geq 1$.
\lim_{z \rightarrow \infty} R(z) \neq 1 \qquad \textrm{and} \qquad \frac{1}{z}(1-R(z)) \; \textrm{ has no zeros in } \; \C^{-} ,
We construct practical diagonally implicit Runge--Kutta (DIRK) methods which attain up to fifth order B-convergence.

Then we consider several PDE test problems that successively deviate further from the assumptions of \cref{sec:math_foundations}, ranging from semilinear PDE (\cref{subsec:numerics_SL_advection,subsec:Allen-Cahn}), to a nonlinear PDE whose highest derivative operators are linear (\cref{subsec:viscous_Burgers}).

issues.failure_explanation: The caption (and the analogous Allen--Cahn caption, plus the introduction's 'attain up to fifth order B-convergence') asserts that the new methods' full-order convergence ($q=p=\psl+1$) is established by the paper's theory. thm:convergence yields $q=\psl+1$ only if $R(z)$ satisfies Eq:Rcondition, and this condition is never verified for the constructed methods (the paper itself notes such conditions can fail, saying of existing methods 'nearly all of these methods satisfy the superconvergence conditions'). Moreover, the EDIRK-(19,5,4) displayed in the same figure is only A(89.8°)-stable and thus fails thm:convergence's A-stability hypothesis outright, and the advection test problem (time-dependent inflow boundary data, non-globally-Lipschitz reaction $u^2$) lies outside Assumption 1, as the paper acknowledges. Unconditionally, the theory guarantees only $q=\psl=p-1$ for these methods on this problem; the full order $p$ is an empirical observation.

failure_location.quote: The new methods consistently exhibit the convergence orders established by the semilinear theory.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either verify Eq:Rcondition for ESDIRK-(8,4,3) and ESDIRK-(10,5,4) (a finite check of the zeros of $b^T(I-zA)^{-1}\mathbbm{1}$ in $\C^-$) and restrict the claims to methods/problems meeting the hypotheses, or hedge the captions and introduction to state that the theory guarantees order $\psl$ while the full order $p$ is observed numerically.
issues.overall_effect: Summary claims (two figure captions and the introduction) attribute more to the theory than it supports for the displayed methods and test problems; the formal results and the empirical findings themselves are unaffected.
issues.title: Claims that observed full-order convergence is 'established by the semilinear theory' rest on unverified or unmet hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The empirical results stand and the overclaim is confined to summary sentences; it can be repaired by a routine finite verification or by hedging, with no loss of formal content.
